additions.text: Calle de la Montera. There is a pharmacy with a green light. A woman in a white coat is at the door.
Hello. I am Marta. I am a pharmacist.
Hello, Marta. Is the pharmacy open?
Yes. I have water, pills and bandages. Do you need anything?
Here you are. And one thing: a man comes every night at three. He is dead. But he wants to pay.
What time does the man come?
Marta says: “he comes every night at three.”
Is there a pharmacy near your home?
What do you have at home for a headache?
Calle del Arenal. A boy on a bike has a yellow backpack. In the backpack there is a cold pizza.
Hi! I am Iván. I am a delivery rider.
Are you working today? Madrid is empty!
Yes. The phone has orders. Look: a pizza for number four, third floor.
And who is on the third floor?
I don’t know. The note says: “Knock hard. We are inside. We are hungry.” I don’t want to go.
Do you order food to your home?
Calle de Bailén. A very old man is on a first-floor balcony. He has a blanket and a coffee.
Good afternoon! I am Don Eusebio. I am eighty-eight years old.
Hello! Are you OK? Are you alone?
I am fine. My wife, Pilar, is on the stairs. She sings every night.
No. Pilar is dead. But she sings. I do not open the door.
He says: “I am eighty-eight years old.”
Does your home have a balcony?
Plaza de España. A blond girl has a map, a suitcase and a phone. The phone has three percent battery.
Hello… My name is Hanna. I am from Germany. I speak a little Spanish.
Hello, Hanna. Where is your group?
I don’t know. The guide has a red flag. Now there is a red flag over there… but the guide does not speak. He only screams.
Don’t go. Come with me to the metro.
Thank you. Madrid is very pretty. But not today.
What city do you want to visit?
Temple of Debod. It is an Egyptian temple in Madrid. A nun prays next to the water.
Good afternoon, child. I am Sister Inés.
Hello, Sister Inés. What are you doing here?
I pray. And I watch. Every afternoon, at eight, they come here.
The dead? And what do they do?
Nothing. They look at the sun. They don’t move. When the sun is gone, they scream.
What time do the dead come?
Sister Inés says: “at eight, they come here.”
Do you like to watch the sun in the evening?
Is there a quiet place in your city?
Calle de Bailén. There is a fence and a young soldier. He has a helmet and a torch.
Calm down. I have the vaccine. I am not sick.
Sorry. I am Rubén. I am a corporal. I am afraid. My colleagues are not here.
Over there, in the Palace. They wear the uniform… but they have white eyes.
Plaza de la Armería. On one side is the Royal Palace. On the other side is the cathedral. A priest is at the door.
Hello. I am Father Tomás. This is my church, the Almudena.
It is very big. Are there people inside?
Yes, twelve living people. But there is a problem: the bells.
What is wrong with the bells?
They ring at twelve at night. Nobody is up there. And the dead come to the square.
How many living people are in the church?
Is there a church in your neighbourhood?
What noises do you hear at night?
Plaza de Oriente. There are statues of kings. A boy plays the guitar. Three dead people are in front of him. They don’t move.
Shhh… Hi. I am Nacho. I play the guitar.
There are three dead people in front of you!
Yes. With music they are calm. They listen.
Without music, they eat. That is why I play. I play all day. My fingers hurt.
Gran Vía. There is a white taxi with a red line. The meter is on. A man is in the front seat.
Hi. I am Fermín. I am a taxi driver.
Because of the passenger. He is in the back. He has his seat belt on.
But… he does not speak. And his face is grey.
Yes. It is nine days. It is three thousand euros. He does not pay.
In the back of the taxi.
Fermín says: “He is in the back. He has his seat belt on.”
Do you take taxis in your city?
Do you have a car or a motorbike?
Calle de Fuencarral. A girl is sitting in a doorway. She has a notebook and a pen.
Hi. I am Lucía. I study medicine.
I write what the virus is like. First: fever. Then: black veins.
Then they don’t remember their name. At the end, they don’t remember their face. Look: my hand. I have a black vein.
What do you study or what did you study?
Do you write in a notebook?
Malasaña. A tattoo studio has its door open. A boy with a beard has a machine in his hand.
Hi! I am Dani. I am a tattoo artist. Do you want a tattoo?
Yes. I write people’s names on their arm. If you die, they know your name.
It is sad. But it is a good idea.
Look at the street. That dead man has a tattoo: “MUM.” That dead man is someone.
What does Dani write on the arm?
Dani says: “I write people’s names on their arm.”
What word is important to you?
Calle de Alcalá. There is an old building. A man in a blue suit is at the door. He has a lot of keys.
Good morning. I am Don Ramón, the doorman.
Good morning. Are there neighbours in the building?
Yes. On the first floor, a family. On the second, a teacher. On the fourth… Mrs Luisa.
No. She knocks on the door all night. Bang, bang, bang. I have the key. I do not open it.
What floor do you live on?
Plaza de Cibeles. There is smoke. A fire truck is in the square. A strong woman has a yellow helmet.
Hi! I am Carmen. I am a firefighter.
Hi, Carmen. Is there a fire?
There is fire all over Madrid. But I have a plan. The siren makes a lot of noise.
And the dead come with the noise…
Exactly. I put the siren in the park. They go to the park. And people run to the hospital.
What makes a lot of noise?
Carmen says: “The siren makes a lot of noise.”
Puerta de Alcalá. An old lady is on a bench. She is knitting. Next to her there is a man tied to the bench.
Good afternoon. I am Amparo. This is Paco, my husband.
I know. But he is my husband. Fifty years together.
And why is he tied up?
Because he bites. But he likes the sun. And I talk to him. It is cold today, Paco.
Do you know an old couple?
Do you like to knit or to cook?
Calle de Alfonso XII. A boy in sports clothes is breathing very fast. He has a watch on his wrist.
Hi… phew… I am Álex. I run every day.
You are running today? There are dead people in the street!
That is why I run. I check the streets and warn people.
Almost all of them. But there are new ones. The new ones run. They run a lot.
What do the new dead do?
Do you do sport every week?
Are you a fast or a slow person?
The Retiro. It is a very big park. A gardener with a straw hat is among the trees.
Hello. I am Julián. I am the Retiro gardener.
Hello, Julián. The trees look strange.
Yes. The leaves are grey. And the green cloud comes out of the Crystal Palace.
Yes. But at night the trees talk. They say my name. “Julián, Julián.”
Do you have plants at home?
Paseo del Prado. In front of the museum there is a woman with a closed umbrella. She is a guide.
Hello. I am Elena. I am a guide at the Prado Museum.
Hello, Elena. Is the museum closed?
Yes. But I sleep inside. There are paintings by Goya. They are black, ugly paintings.
A little. In one painting, a giant eats a person. Now the street is like the painting.
Paseo del Prado. A man with an easel is painting. In the picture there is a grey face with white eyes.
Hi. My name is Ernesto. I paint.
Yes. They are people. They have names. This is Rosa. She sells flowers in Atocha.
It is a very pretty painting. And very sad.
Thank you. I paint fast. Rosa does not wait long.
Do you like drawing or painting?
Do you have photos of your family?
Calle de Felipe IV. There is a big lorry. A man is on top, on the roof, with an iron bar.
Who are you? I am Manolo. This is my lorry.
Hi, Manolo. What is in the lorry?
Food. Bread, milk, fruit. A lot of food.
No. It is for the people in the hospital. Take an apple. They don’t eat fruit.
For the people in the hospital.
Manolo says: “It is for the people in the hospital.”
What do you eat in the morning?
Near Atocha. A young woman has a baby in her arms. The baby is sleeping. She speaks very quietly.
Shhh. Hi. I am Rocío. This is Leo. He is three months old.
Yes. I need milk for him. And a safe place.
There are people in the hospital. And there is milk.
Thank you. But please, don’t speak loudly. If Leo cries, they come.
Do you have children or nephews and nieces?
How many hours do you sleep?
Ronda de Atocha. A man with a cap and a train uniform is in the street. He has a ticket machine.
I know. I am Sergio. I am a ticket inspector. I ask for tickets. It is my job.
In the tunnel. It is the seven o’clock train to Valencia. The lights are on. And the people are inside. Still.
Sergio says: “the seven o’clock train to Valencia.”
Ronda de Atocha. A girl goes past very fast on skates. She stops in front of you. She has a paper in her hand.
Hi! I am Vega. I carry messages.
There is no internet. I carry papers from one street to another. I am very fast.
It says: “Don’t go to Lavapiés. Don’t look them in the eyes.” It is for you too.
Can you skate or ride a bike?
How do you get to work or class?
Near the river. A big man in an apron is next to a butcher’s shop. It smells very bad.
Hi. I am Andrés. I am a butcher.
It is old meat. The dead like it a lot. I put it in the street, far from the people.
What a good idea! And do you eat meat?
Not any more. Now I only eat vegetables. It is strange, right?
Andrés says: “Now I only eat vegetables.”
Do you eat meat or are you vegetarian?
Calle de Toledo. A boy looks at the faces of the dead through binoculars. He has a photo of two identical boys.
Hi. I am Hugo. I am looking for my brother. His name is Leo. We are twins.
Does he look exactly like you?
Yes. The same. The same face, the same hair.
I don’t know. But look over there, among the dead. There is a boy with my face… and with white eyes.
Do you have brothers or sisters?
Who in your family do you look like?
The Manzanares river. A man is sitting on a chair. He is fishing. Next to him there is a bucket of water.
Hi. I am Benito. I fish here every day.
Are there fish in the river?
Yes. Look at the bucket. I have two fish.
Yes. They all have green eyes now. And look at the river: something is pulling the rod. Something big.
What colour are the fish’s eyes?
The mascot says: “They have green eyes!”
Is there a river in your city?
Calle del Arenal, near the Teatro Real. A woman in a long dress is at a window. She sings very loudly.
Aaaah! … Oh, hi. I am Sofía. I am an opera singer.
Yes. With my voice, the dead cover their ears. And they go away.
Great! Do you sing all day?
No. My throat hurts. Tonight I have no voice. And the door is old.
Carrera de San Jerónimo. A boy with glasses is in a car with three computers. The screens show the street.
Hi. I am Pablo. I work in IT. I watch the Madrid cameras.
Yes. Look at this one. It is three thirty-three. All the dead stop.
They stop? And what do they do?
They look at the camera. All of them. At the same time. They look at me.
What time do the dead stop?
Pablo says: “It is three thirty-three. All the dead stop.”
Do you use the computer a lot?
How many hours do you look at your phone?
A street near Sol. There is a hair salon with a broken mirror. A woman has some scissors.
Hi, handsome. I am Yolanda. I am a hairdresser. Sit down.
Yes. Short hair, very short. The dead grab you by the hair.
Very good. Don’t look in the mirror. Sometimes there is someone behind you.
Do you have long or short hair?
How often do you go to the hairdresser?
A doorway near Sol. A man with a long beard is sitting on some cardboard. He has a small dog.
Hi. I am Ginés. I live here. This is Chispa, my dog.
Hi, Ginés. Aren’t you afraid in the street?
No. The dead do not look at me. They walk past me.
I don’t know. To people, I am invisible. To the dead, too. It is the same.
Ginés says: “This is Chispa, my dog.”
Do you have a pet at home?
A street near Gran Vía. A tall girl in athletics clothes is sitting on the ground. She has a bandage on her arm.
Hi. I am Irene. I am an athlete. I run the four hundred metres.
Hi, Irene. What do you have on your arm?
Nothing. It is… a dog. Yes, a dog.
Irene, I have the vaccine. I can help you.
Really? I am very hot. And very hungry. Please, quickly.
Do you have a small secret?
What sport do you like to watch?
